subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Seldom if ever has there been an instance (1)/ where opposition was treated (2)/ with such organizational neglect (3)/ as seen today. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect placement of the phrase "**if ever**" after "**Seldom**."
 
• The phrase "**Seldom if ever**" is not typically used as it creates a redundancy in meaning.
 
• The correct construction should be "**Seldom has there been an instance**," removing the phrase "if ever" to ensure clarity and correctness.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Seldom has there been an instance where opposition was treated with such organizational neglect as seen today."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 2: "where opposition was treated"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 3: "with such organizational neglect"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 4: "as seen today"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
